# Private cones: radial balancing fails without angular separation

This note gives two complementary bounded results for a full-rank
concurrent cap group. Equal positive radial-height distributions do not
force any dimension-only amount of double-covered mass, even for actual
convex fibers containing a common interior point. On the other hand,
an explicit angular-slack and radial-window condition permits the finite
parity transport lemma and gives an exact retained-volume bound.

No ordinary or mixed center theorem is inferred. In particular the
counterexample below is not a counterexample to the mixed depth target.

## 1. A rational rectangle with balanced private masses and tiny overlap

In continuous coordinates (t,s) in R^2 use the margins

    h_1=t+s, h_2=-t+s, h_0=-2s.

They sum to zero, have rank two, and define a concurrent three-cap
cover H_i={h_i>=0} of all R^2. Let U_i be the region where h_i is
positive and both other margins are negative. Margin-zero lines have
area zero, so choosing weak inequalities for the positive margin does
not change any area below.

For L>=2 and epsilon=L^(-2), let

    K_L={|t|<=L, -epsilon<=s<=1}.

The origin lies strictly inside K_L. Its area W and private areas are

    W=2L(1+epsilon),
    |K_L intersect U_1|=|K_L intersect U_2|=L-1/2,
    |K_L intersect U_0|=epsilon^2.                     (1)

Indeed U_1 on this rectangle has 0<s<1 and s<t<L; U_2 is its reflection.
For U_0, -epsilon<s<0 and s<t<-s. The area covered by at least two caps is

    D_L=W-sum_i |K_L intersect U_i|
       =1+2L epsilon-epsilon^2.                        (2)

There is no positive-area triple-covered set, since the margins sum to
zero. Thus

    D_L/(L-1/2) -> 0.

This rules out every positive constant c, even in fixed dimension two,
in a claim that double-covered area is at least
c Phi_2(|K intersect U_1|,|K intersect U_2|). The two arguments of Phi
are equal here, so Phi equals L-1/2.

The failure persists after exact radial-height balancing. Consider

    P_+={L/2<=t<=L, 1/2<=s<=1},
    P_-={-L<=t<=-L/2, 1/2<=s<=1}.

Up to boundary lines, these lie in U_1 and U_2, respectively, and each
has area L/4. Reflection (t,s)->(-t,s) pushes their uniform measures
onto each other and identifies the positive heights h_1 on P_+ and
h_2 on P_-. Their height distributions are EXACTLY identical and lie
in [L/2+1/2,L+1], an interval with endpoint ratio exactly two.

If x=(t,s) in P_+ and y=(t',s') in P_- have equal positive heights,
then t+s=-t'+s', so the t-coordinate of their midpoint is (s'-s)/2.
Every such balanced midpoint therefore belongs to the double-covered
rectangle

    {|t|<=1/4, 1/2<=s<=1},

of area 1/4. Any measure supported on these midpoints and bounded by
ordinary area can have mass at most 1/4, whereas each source has mass
L/4. There is consequently no universal positive retained-mass fraction
for a density-at-most-one, equal-height midpoint transport. This is an
angular cancellation obstruction, not merely a disparity of radial
lengths or of the two height laws.

## 2. An actual source with all global cap fractions below one half

The obstruction can coexist with a proper low-fraction whole-space cap
group. Let

    S=[[ -1/2,-3/2 ],[ 1/2,-1/2 ]].

It has determinant one, S^3=I, and cyclically permutes the three margins:
(h_1,h_2,h_0)(Sx)=(h_0,h_1,h_2)(x). Put the three bodies
K_L, S K_L, S^2 K_L at the three integer bases

    (0,0), (1,0), (0,1)

and take their Cayley hull C in R^2 times R^2. The base unit triangle
contains exactly those three integer points, all exposed. Hence these
are the EXACT actual integer fibers. Their areas are all W, C is full
dimensional, and C equals the convex hull of its actual mixed set.
The origin is interior to every real fiber: each generating body contains
a common small ball about zero, and so do their convex interpolations.

Let E_total be the mixed mass covered at least twice. Cyclic invariance
and (2) give

    M=3W, E_total=3D_L,
    B_0=B_1=B_2=W+D_L,
    B_i/M=(1+D_L/W)/3 -> 1/3.                          (3)

For the equality of cap budgets, the sum of the three cap areas on one
fiber is W+D_L; rotation makes each global cap collect precisely this
sum. Every cap is proper on every fiber. Since L>=2 and epsilon=L^(-2),

    D_L < W/2,

because W/2-D_L=L-1-1/L+1/L^4>0. Thus all three global cap fractions are
strictly below one half. Also the total private mass in each label is
W-D_L. Nevertheless E_total/M tends to zero. In the parity class of the
first base, the two private masses from (1) already diverge while the
GLOBAL double-covered mass remains bounded. Thus no dimension-only
bridge bound using these unrestricted private masses can hold even with
actual convex compatibility, equal global budgets, a full-rank group,
and a common affine interior section.

This cap group is not asserted to be a critical maximum-depth cover.
The example is explicitly OC-safe: the ordinary centroid of any one
fiber, placed at its base, has actual mixed depth at least
Gamma_2/3=4/27>Gamma_2/4=1/9, since its own fiber alone supplies that
amount to every containing ambient halfspace. The common meeting point
zero need not be such a centroid.

## 3. A valid angular-window bridge

For a general full-rank concurrent group of d+1 caps, d>=2, incorporate
the positive dependence coefficients into the margins so that

    sum_(i=0)^d h_i=0.

Scaling each margin positively preserves its cap. When the group's
common meeting section q(z) is affine and lies in the relevant fibers,
it may be moved to zero by an affine-in-base continuous shear; after
that shear the h_i are linear in the continuous coordinate alone.
The next window statement only needs convex
compatibility; the common section is used for contractions in Section 4.

Fix distinct labels i,j, an angular slack eta in (0,1), and a ratio

    1<=q<=1/(1-eta).

At each integer base z choose a convex measurable source piece A_z in
the closed private cone i, and B_z in the closed private cone j, with

    H<=h_i(x)<=qH,    -h_j(x)<=(1-eta)h_i(x)  on A_z,
    H<=h_j(y)<=qH,    -h_i(y)<=(1-eta)h_j(y)  on B_z,    (4)

where H>0 is common. Other margins on each piece are nonpositive.
Using closures instead of strict private cones only adds sets of
d-volume zero. Define A_r=sum_(z parity r)|A_z| and B_r analogously.

Every midpoint of an A-piece and a B-piece satisfies

    h_i((x+y)/2), h_j((x+y)/2)
       >= [1-(1-eta)q]H/2 >= 0,
    h_l((x+y)/2)<=0 for l different from i,j.            (5)

Thus the entire midpoint lies in the region with precisely this pair
of nonnegative margins, up to zero-volume boundary hyperplanes.
For a parity with A_r B_r>0, the collision-free finite transport lemma
and actual midpoint inclusion give

    sum_z |K_z intersect {h_i>=0,h_j>=0,h_l<=0 (l!=i,j)}|
       >= Phi_d(A_r,B_r).                              (6)

The conclusion uses ONE original cap group, not independently selected
continuous normals. It includes all integer target bases and all
nonnegative/zero boundary conventions through actual d-volume.

One may choose different source pieces, windows and slacks for different
unordered label pairs. The corresponding exactly-two-covered regions
are disjoint outside finitely many hyperplanes. Consequently their
bounds can be summed over pairs, taking the strongest parity bound for
each pair, just as in the simplex-vertex neighborhood bridge theorem.
One must not sum different parities for the SAME pair without a target
collision argument.

## 4. Exact cost of radial contraction into a common window

Suppose zero belongs to every relevant actual fiber. In the preceding
construction, permit the positive-height window of a piece A_z to be
[a_z,q a_z] rather than [H,qH], with a_z>0. Choose H<=min_z a_z and
replace A_z by (H/a_z)A_z. Convexity and zero in K_z put the replacement
inside the SAME actual fiber; it retains its private cone and angular
slack and now satisfies the common window condition. Its exact volume is

    (H/a_z)^d |A_z|.

Do the same for the j-pieces, with possibly different lower heights b_z,
using H no larger than any selected a_z or b_z. The valid right side of
(6) is then Phi_d applied to the explicit retained parity masses

    H^d sum_(z parity r) |A_z|/a_z^d,
    H^d sum_(z parity r) |B_z|/b_z^d.                  (7)

Choose at most one piece per label and base in this formula, or otherwise
account for overlaps of multiple contracted pieces. No sum of their
volumes is justified merely because their original pieces were disjoint.
The factor (H/a_z)^d is the exact homothety Jacobian, not an unspecified
loss. Both geometric conditions are necessary for this particular
argument: radial contraction pays for height mismatch, while (5) pays
for angular separation. The balanced rectangle pieces in Section 1 show
why equal height laws alone cannot replace the latter condition.

## 5. Verification and scope

The exact stdlib verifier
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_private_cone_radial_balancing_and_window_bridge.py` checks the
rectangle cap/private/overlap areas by rational polygon clipping, the
cyclic matrix and equal-budget source, the equal-height matching bounds,
and the linear angular-window margins and homothety costs.

This closes the unqualified dimension-only radial-balancing claim and
provides a conditioned replacement with explicit retained masses. It
does not say how much arbitrary source mass satisfies a fixed positive
angular slack; the counterexample proves that fraction can vanish.
